abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide (ERCO 2 ) driven by non-conventional sources of energy is a favorable approach to generate closed loop CO 2 cycle. It will reduce CO 2 emissions by lowering CO 2 levels in the atmosphere and converting it into high-energy-density carbon-based fuels like alcohols and hydrocarbons. Monometallic copper based catalysts are largely reported for ERCO 2 to a variety of industrially important carbon products. But, challenges such as high over potential, uncontrollable product selectivity, and catalyst deactivation inhibit their progress. Oxide derived bimetallic CuZn x electrocatalysts have been suggested as alternatives for achieving high selectivity for different valuable products. In this study, the co-precipitation approach has been used to prepare CuO with various quantities of ZnO dopants. HRTEM, FESEM, XRD, and XPS were used to conduct detailed morphological and elemental studies on the electrode. The electrochemical performance was measured using H-type electrochemical cell in aqueous 0.1 M KHCO 3 electrolyte. The evaluation of different CuO-ZnO x (where x = 5, 10, 15 and 20 wt.%) catalysts for ethanol productivity and Faradaic efficiency are of particular importance. Amongst studied electrocatalysts, the highest Faradaic efficiency of 22.27 % was obtained for ethanol using CuO-ZnO 10 at -0.80 V (vs RHE) with the production rate of about 121 μmol h −1 L −1 . The optimized electrode (CuO-ZnO 10 ) shows long term stability for at least 12 h. Post characterization of the catalyst was also conducted to obtain an insight into the active sites, which indicated that CO 2 reduction took place on reduced oxide sites (i.e. metallic sites) rather than metal oxides. © 2021 Elsevier Ltd. Different bimetallic electrocatalysts have been reported in the iterature like, CuAg [21] , CuPd [19] , CuAu [22] , etc. Unfortunately, g, Pd, and Au lack the strong binding of ∗CO intermediates which ead to loss of deep reduction products like ethanol. On the other
and, Cu with Zn shows suppression of HERs and promotes multiarbon products with higher selectivity [18] . Also, Zn is more enironmentally benign and affordable as compared to different coatalysts like Ag, Pd, and Au. Li et. al. [23] reported the effect f composition and geometric structure of CuO-ZnO catalysts for he selective production of C 2 H 4 and C 2 H 5 OH. Using 8CuO/2ZnO/C lectrocatalyst, 24.0 % Faradaic efficiency (FE) was achieved at -0.75
vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). According to their reort, the reduced ZnO nanoparticles supply extra CO to reduced uO nanoparticles which increase the ∗CO surface coverage for Ccoupling. The uniform distribution of Cu and Zn atoms in the lectrocatalysts was found to enhance CO spillover effects. Su et. l. [24] reported hierarchically mesoporous-macroporous (HMMP) u/Zn alloy catalysts for liquid C2 products. Optimized HMMP u5Zn8 electrocatalyst exhibited a very high ethanol selectivity of 6.6 % and ethanol current density (J ethanol ) of -2.3 mA cm −2 at
0.8 V (vs. RHE) and excellent stability of 11 h towards ERCO 2 . ratzel and group [25] demonstrated in-situ electrochemical reuction method for the synthesis of CuZn bimetallic catalysts from nO-shell/CuO-core bi-metal-oxide. This CuZn bimetallic catalysts eveal 31.5 % FE for ethanol production with J ethanol of −10.5 mA m −2 at -1.15 V (vs. RHE). Ren et al. [26] also reported oxide deived Cu with different amounts of Zn dopants for ERCO 2 to liquid uels. Cu4Zn catalyst shows improved FE of 29.1 % for ethanol with total of -8.2 mA cm −2 at −1.05 V (vs. RHE). Cu4Zn catalyst also howed long term stability of 5 h for ethanol production.
In the earlier work, metallic Cu nanoparticles (Cu NPs) [27] , u NPs on N-doped graphene (Cu x /NGN) [16] , and oxide-derived u-Zn nanoparticles supported on N-doped graphene [28] were sed for the ERCO 2 with an aim to produce ethanol. Further, the electrocatalysts with high deree of surface heterogeneity and availability of multiple adjaent active sites to facilitate the stabilization of different adsorbed eaction intermediates, the copper supported on nitrogen doped raphene (Cu x /NGN) Cu NPs were used for ethanol production 16] . The twenty wt.% copper on NGN showed uniform dispersion f Cu on NGN and produced ethanol with 25.72 % FE at -1.0 V vs. RHE).

orted on N-doped graphene has been also reported in our ear-

n precursor, respectively. The loading percentage of Cu to Zn in he electrocatalysts can be easily adjusted by changing the preursor concentrations. The activity and selectivity of synthesized uO-ZnO x were studied by various electrochemical characterizaion methods.

.4. Preparation of the working electrode
Initially, the mixture of catalyst powder (4 mg), Nafion® 117 soution (30 μL) and isopropanol (1 mL) was sonicated for 30 min for ts uniform distribution. Obtained mixture is also called as catalyst nk. This catalyst ink was then sprayed onto a carbon paper using

To shed light on the kinetic mechanism of the ERCO 2 over the uO-ZnO x electrodes, a plot of the log of the overall current denity versus the potential (Tafel plot) was obtained by LSV data 34 , 40 ].
